source.title: The Emergence of Reproducibility and Generalizability in Diffusion Models
source.authors: Huijie Zhang; Jinfan Zhou; Yifu Lu; Minzhe Guo; Peng Wang; Liyue Shen; Qing Qu

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures similarity between diffusion-model outputs generated from shared noise, not similarity between internal representations or distances induced on shared inputs. Its results therefore do not test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own output-reproducibility results, recorded below as findings about a related but different construct. It also cites work on representation reproducibility in related works; those cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper measures how similar the generated images are when different diffusion models start from the same initial noise. This is the similarity of the noise-to-image mapping, judged by SSCD and MAE on outputs. It does not compare internal representations, so it does not measure alignment, mapping, stitching, shared features or metric dependence of representations. The authors link it to identifiable encoding and cite Li+15 (an original source), but their own results concern a related but different construct. The findings are therefore recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that, given the same noise and a deterministic sampler, different diffusion models produce near-identical outputs across architectures, training and sampling procedures and perturbation kernels. They attribute this to the models learning the same score function: of the empirical distribution in the memorization regime and of the underlying distribution in the generalization regime. They also report that the property is rare in GANs and VAEs, and that it extends in structured, conditional ways to conditional models, inverse problems (within an architecture family) and fine-tuning. They make no claim about internal representations converging with scale.
record.recipe_differences: The paper's output-reproducibility experiment is not a test of the original representation-alignment methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Output reproducibility varies with the similarity metric and threshold, initial noise, conditional class, inverse-problem observation and task difficulty, architecture category, and fine-tuning regime.

fits_no_version.finding: Different diffusion models generate similar images from the same initial noise; similarity varies across model pairs and settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Diffusion models trained on the same data learn a near-identical noise-to-image mapping (output reproducibility).

fits_no_version.finding: In inverse-problem sampling, reproducibility depends on architecture category, observation and task difficulty.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output reproducibility in diffusion inverse problems holds mainly within an architecture family.

fits_no_version.finding: Partial fine-tuning lowers reproducibility in the memorization regime; its effect is minor in the generalization regime.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training regime and fine-tuning strategy affect diffusion output reproducibility.

fits_no_version.finding: GANs (wGAN, SNGAN) and VAEs (VAE, VAMP) show little cross-model reproducibility (Figure 3). Reproducibility is high in both the memorization and generalization regimes, with a phase transition between them (Figures 1 and 4). No rows record these results.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shared-noise output reproducibility is specific to diffusion models and arises in two data-size regimes.

record.problems: The reported results concern generated-output similarity rather than internal representations. Most model-comparison values are presented in figures, and no uncertainty estimates are reported. Several conclusions are based on a fixed prompt, selected observations, or specified sampling settings.

untested.parts: No measure of internal representation alignment across model scale or capability.
No comparison of features or subspaces across seeds.
No mapping, stitching or relative representation between internal representations. Output-level similarity only.
No interpretable features or circuits examined.
The output-similarity thresholds vary, but representation-similarity metrics are not varied.
Output similarity is attributed to shared training data (SD v1-3/v1-4), but this concerns outputs, not representation alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The rows_left_out statement is inaccurate: the GAN/VAE contrast (Figure 3), the regime phase transition (Figures 1 and 4) and ImageNet conditional reproducibility (Figure 9) are not recorded. None bears on a claim version, so none goes in missing. The states on none-version rows are informational only.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not measure internal representation alignment as model size or capability changes.
No paired image-caption representations or alignment trends with model quality are measured.
The paper does not compare internal features or shared subspaces across random seeds.
Shared-noise output similarity is measured, but no mapping between internal representations, stitching, or relative representations is tested.
The paper does not examine recurring interpretable features or circuits.
The paper varies output-similarity metrics and some generation settings, not representation-similarity metrics, their settings, or input distributions.
The paper does not test whether representation alignment is incomplete or explained by shared training data or objectives.
